title: Simple Resignation Letter Template
description: Free professional resignation letter template for employees leaving a job. Copy, customize, and submit your formal resignation with this straightforward, respectful resignation letter.
intro: A Simple Resignation Letter is a brief, professional document used to formally notify your employer of your intent to leave a position. This template provides a straightforward, respectful format that maintains professionalism while clearly communicating your resignation effective date. It is suitable for most employment situations and can be customized for various industries and seniority levels.
whenToUse: Use this template when leaving a job and providing formal written notice of resignation. It works well for straightforward departures, career changes, relocations, or other standard resignation situations where you want to keep the letter concise and professional.
template:
Dear [Manager Name],

I am writing to formally resign from my position as [Your Job Title] at [Company Name], effective [Last Working Day, MM/DD/YYYY].

I have valued my time working with the team and appreciate the opportunities for professional growth and development. Your guidance and support have contributed to my professional development.

During my remaining time, I am committed to ensuring a smooth transition. I am available to assist with knowledge transfer, training my replacement, or addressing any outstanding projects as needed.

Thank you for the opportunities and experiences I have gained during my tenure. I wish you and the company continued success.

Sincerely,
[Your Full Name]
[Your Contact Information]
example:
Dear Mr. Smith,

I am writing to formally resign from my position as Marketing Coordinator at ABC Corp, effective March 30, 2026.

I have valued my time working with the team and appreciate the professional development opportunities. Your guidance has been instrumental in my career growth.

During my remaining two weeks, I am committed to ensuring a smooth transition. I am available to train my replacement and complete current projects as needed.

Thank you for the opportunities and experiences during my time at ABC Corp. I wish you and the company continued success.

Sincerely,
John Doe
(555) 123-4567
john.doe@email.com
tips: Keep the tone professional, grateful, and positive—avoid complaining about your job or company.
Provide a specific last working day (typically two weeks from submission) to allow for transition planning.
Offer to help with the transition and knowledge transfer to demonstrate professionalism.
Deliver the letter in person first if possible, then follow up with email or formal submission.
Mention specific skills or experiences you gained rather than generic praise.
Keep the letter to one page and maintain a respectful tone throughout.
Double-check spelling and grammar before submitting.
Keep a copy of your resignation letter for your personal employment records.

faqs.question: How much notice should I give when resigning?
faqs.answer: Two weeks' notice is standard in most industries. However, check your employment contract or company policy for specific requirements. Some positions, especially senior roles, may require more notice.

faqs.question: Should a resignation letter be formal?
faqs.answer: Yes. Professional resignation letters help maintain positive relationships with employers, protect your professional reputation, and ensure proper documentation of your departure.

faqs.question: Can I resign by email instead of a formal letter?
faqs.answer: While many employers accept resignation notices by email, it's best practice to deliver a formal letter in person first and then follow up via email. Check your company's HR policies.

faqs.question: What if I'm being forced to resign?
faqs.answer: If you're being pressured to resign under unfavorable circumstances, consult an employment attorney or labor board before submitting a resignation. Document all communications.

faqs.question: Should I include reasons for leaving in my resignation letter?
faqs.answer: It's optional to include reasons. A simple resignation letter can focus purely on the fact and date of resignation. Longer letters can briefly mention new opportunities or personal circumstances if desired.

faqs.question: What happens after I submit a resignation letter?
faqs.answer: Your employer will typically acknowledge receipt, discuss your transition, outline your final responsibilities, and begin the knowledge transfer process. Your final paycheck and benefits information should also be addressed.

faqs.question: Can I resign verbally without a written letter?
faqs.answer: While verbal resignation is sometimes acceptable, always follow up with a written letter. Written documentation protects both you and your employer and provides a clear record of your resignation date.

faqs.question: Is it ever appropriate to resign immediately without notice?
faqs.answer: Immediate resignation should only occur in situations of severe harassment, unsafe working conditions, or breach of employment agreement. Provide notice when possible to maintain professional relationships.

title: Two Weeks Notice Letter Template
description: Free two weeks notice letter template for professionally resigning from a job with proper advance notice. Includes formal resignation letter format and resignation procedures.
intro: A Two Weeks Notice Letter is the standard professional way to inform your employer that you're resigning while giving them adequate time to prepare for your departure. This template provides a formal, respectful resignation letter that clearly communicates your final working day and demonstrates your commitment to a smooth transition. The two-week notice period is the industry standard and allows employers time to post your position, interview candidates, and manage the transition of your responsibilities.
whenToUse: Use this template when resigning from a job with the intention of providing the standard two weeks of advance notice. It is appropriate for most employment situations, particularly when you want to leave on good terms and maintain professional relationships.
template:
Dear [Manager Name],

Please accept this letter as formal notice of my resignation from my position as [Your Job Title] at [Company Name]. My final working day will be [Last Working Day, MM/DD/YYYY], providing two weeks' notice as of today.

I have truly appreciated the opportunities for professional growth and the collaborative relationships I have built during my tenure. Working with the team has been valuable, and I am grateful for the experiences and skills I have developed here.

During my two weeks' notice period, I am committed to ensuring a smooth and professional transition. I am available to:

- Document my current projects and ongoing responsibilities
- Train my replacement or other team members
- Complete critical deliverables and hand off work appropriately
- Organize files and transfer necessary documentation

Thank you for the opportunity to contribute to the organization. I wish you and the team continued success.

Sincerely,
[Your Full Name]
[Your Phone Number]
[Your Email Address]
example:
Dear Ms. Johnson,

Please accept this letter as formal notice of my resignation from my position as Project Manager at Bright Solutions. My final working day will be April 14, 2026, providing two weeks' notice as of today.

I have truly appreciated the opportunities for professional development and the collaborative relationships I have built here. Working with this team has been a rewarding experience.

During my notice period, I am committed to:

- Documenting all current projects and timelines
- Training the team on critical processes
- Completing the quarterly report deliverables
- Transferring all client relationships documentation

Thank you for the opportunity to contribute to Bright Solutions. I wish you and the team continued success.

Sincerely,
Sarah Lee
(555) 987-6543
sarah.lee@email.com
tips: Submit your two-week notice letter in person first whenever possible, followed by email documentation.
Calculate exactly two weeks from the submission date and verify this date before writing the letter.
Be specific about your final working day rather than using vague language.
Offer concrete ways you will help with the transition rather than generic statements.
Maintain a professional, grateful tone even if you're leaving due to negative circumstances.
Proofread carefully and avoid typos, grammatical errors, or emotional language.
Keep a copy for your personal records and request written acknowledgment from your employer.
Discuss benefits continuation, final paycheck timing, and reference policies separately with HR.

faqs.question: What is a two weeks notice letter?
faqs.answer: A two weeks notice letter is a formal document informing your employer of your resignation with 14 days' advance notice, allowing time for transition planning and replacement recruitment.

faqs.question: Do all jobs require two weeks notice?
faqs.answer: Policies vary by employer and employment agreement. Check your contract or employee handbook. Some positions require more notice, and some states have specific notice requirements. However, two weeks is the professional standard.

faqs.question: What should I include in a two weeks notice letter?
faqs.answer: Include your position title, the exact final working day, gratitude for the opportunity, a commitment to transition assistance, and professional contact information. Keep it concise and positive.

faqs.question: Can I resign immediately without providing two weeks notice?
faqs.answer: You can resign immediately, but this may violate your employment agreement, impact severance or benefits, and damage professional relationships. Provide notice when possible.

faqs.question: Should I discuss my resignation verbally first before submitting a letter?
faqs.answer: Best practice is to discuss your resignation in a private conversation with your manager first, then follow up with a formal written letter. This shows respect and professionalism.

faqs.question: What if my employer asks me to leave immediately after I give two weeks notice?
faqs.answer: Some employers may ask you to leave sooner or offer severance. You can negotiate, but they may invoke an immediate termination clause in your employment agreement. Consult HR or an employment attorney if unsure.

faqs.question: Can my employer require more than two weeks notice?
faqs.answer: Yes, if your employment contract specifies a longer notice period or if you're in a senior leadership position. Always check your contract before determining your notice period.

faqs.question: Should I mention where I'm going next in my resignation letter?
faqs.answer: It's optional to mention your next employer, but keep it brief and professional. Focus on what you're grateful for rather than where you're going.

title: Short Notice Resignation Letter Template
description: Free short notice resignation letter template for employees resigning with limited advance notice. Professional template for emergency departures, health issues, or sudden job changes.
intro: A Short Notice Resignation Letter is used when you must resign with less than the standard two-week notice period. This template provides a professional, concise format for situations requiring immediate or very short notice departures, such as health emergencies, family relocations, or unforeseen circumstances. While short notice can create challenges for employers, a professional letter demonstrates respect and may help preserve your professional reputation.
whenToUse: Use this template when resigning with less than two weeks' notice due to emergencies, health issues, family matters, sudden opportunities, or unavoidable circumstances. It works for situations where providing standard notice is impossible or impractical.
template:
Dear [Manager Name],

I am writing to formally notify you of my resignation from my position as [Your Job Title] at [Company Name], effective [Last Working Day, MM/DD/YYYY].

I understand that short notice creates challenges for the team, and I sincerely regret any disruption this may cause. Unfortunately, [brief reason: unforeseen circumstances have made my immediate departure necessary / a family emergency requires my attention / urgent personal matters require my focus].

I am committed to making this transition as smooth as possible given the circumstances. I am available to:

- Brief team members on urgent projects and priorities
- Provide documentation of critical information
- Assist remotely if needed during the transition

I appreciate the opportunities I have had during my time with [Company Name] and apologize for the short notice.

Sincerely,
[Your Full Name]
[Your Phone Number]
[Your Email Address]
example:
Dear Mr. Evans,

I am writing to formally notify you of my resignation from my position as Regional Sales Manager at Bright Services, effective immediately.

I understand that short notice creates challenges for the team, and I sincerely regret any disruption this may cause. However, a family emergency requires my immediate attention and relocation.

I am committed to making this transition as smooth as possible. I am available to brief my replacement on current accounts and can provide detailed documentation of client relationships and ongoing projects if needed.

I appreciate the professional opportunities I have had and apologize for the abruptness of this departure.

Sincerely,
Dana Lee
(555) 246-8135
dana.lee@email.com
tips: Only use short notice resignation when absolutely necessary—it can damage professional relationships.
Provide a brief, honest explanation for the urgency without oversharing personal details.
Offer specific assistance to help mitigate the impact on your team.
Call your manager before submitting the letter if possible to discuss the situation.
Document your resignation in writing even if you've had a verbal conversation.
Offer to provide important documentation, contact lists, or procedures remotely.
Be prepared that employers may escort you from the premises or ask you to leave immediately.
Follow up after your departure with any promised documentation or transition help.

faqs.question: Is short notice acceptable?
faqs.answer: It depends on your employment agreement and employer policies. While not ideal, short notice may be acceptable in emergency situations. Be prepared for potential consequences regarding references, severance, or final pay.

faqs.question: Can an employer force me to stay longer than I want?
faqs.answer: Employment is typically at-will, meaning you can resign anytime. However, breaching an employment contract's notice requirement may result in legal action or loss of benefits. Consult your contract.

faqs.question: How will short notice affect my final paycheck?
faqs.answer: Your employer must pay all wages owed through your final date. Short notice doesn't typically affect payment, but unused vacation or benefits may be affected based on company policy.

faqs.question: Will short notice damage my professional reputation?
faqs.answer: It can, depending on circumstances. If it's truly an emergency, most professionals understand. However, leaving suddenly without good reason may result in poor references or negative word-of-mouth in your industry.

faqs.question: What should I do if my employer gets angry about short notice?
faqs.answer: Remain professional and calm. Offer to help with transition if possible. If your employer becomes abusive or hostile, it may be best to leave for your safety and well-being.

faqs.question: Can I resign verbally for short notice or do I need a written letter?
faqs.answer: Always provide a written letter even with short notice. It creates an official record of your resignation date and reason, which protects both you and your employer.

faqs.question: What if my employer asks me to stay longer than my short notice period?
faqs.answer: You can refuse. While they may ask you to stay, you are not obligated to remain. However, refusing may affect severance, final pay timing, or references depending on your agreement.

faqs.question: Should I offer to help with transition even if I have to leave immediately?
faqs.answer: Yes, offering remote assistance or available documentation shows professionalism and may preserve your reputation despite the difficult circumstances.

title: Long Form Resignation Letter Template
description: Comprehensive resignation letter template for detailed departures. Professional long-form resignation letter with space for detailed explanation of departure, gratitude, and transition assistance.
intro: A Long Form Resignation Letter is a more detailed, comprehensive resignation document that goes beyond the basics to provide context, express gratitude, and outline transition plans. This template is ideal for employees in senior positions, those with significant tenure, or situations where a more thorough explanation benefits both the employee and employer. The longer format allows for expressing sincere appreciation and demonstrating commitment to a professional transition.
whenToUse: Use this template when you are in a senior position, have worked at the company for many years, want to provide detailed transition planning, or when circumstances warrant a more comprehensive explanation of your departure.
template:
Dear [Manager Name and Company Leadership],

I am writing to formally resign from my position as [Your Job Title] at [Company Name], effective [Last Working Day, MM/DD/YYYY].

After careful consideration, I have decided that it is time for me to pursue a new opportunity / chapter in my career / personal goals. [Optional: briefly explain reason for departure - e.g., "a role aligned with my long-term career objectives" or "the ability to relocate closer to family."]

My tenure at [Company Name] has been incredibly rewarding, and I am genuinely grateful for the professional growth and relationships I have developed. Specifically, I want to acknowledge:

- The mentorship and leadership development I received from [Manager/Leadership]
- The opportunity to lead [specific project/team] and contribute to [specific achievement]
- The collaborative culture and the strong team I've had the privilege to work with
- The professional skills and experiences that will serve me throughout my career

During my final [two weeks / month / period], I am committed to ensuring the smoothest possible transition:

- I will document all ongoing projects, timelines, and status updates
- I am available to train my replacement or team members on critical processes
- I will provide comprehensive handoff documentation of my responsibilities
- I will assist in recruiting and onboarding my successor if possible
- I am available for consultation after my departure if needed

The relationships and experiences I've gained here have been invaluable, and I carry these lessons forward. I have tremendous respect for [Company Name] and its mission, and I wish the organization continued success.

Thank you for the opportunity to contribute to this organization's success. Please let me know how I can best support the transition during my remaining time.

Sincerely,
[Your Full Name]
[Your Phone Number]
[Your Email Address]
[Your LinkedIn Profile - Optional]
example:
Dear Ms. Chen and Leadership Team,

I am writing to formally resign from my position as Senior Marketing Manager at InnovateTech Solutions, effective June 30, 2026.

After careful consideration, I have decided to accept a leadership position with a nonprofit organization focused on environmental sustainability. This role aligns with my long-term career goals and personal passion for making a social impact.

My six years at InnovateTech have been incredibly rewarding, and I am genuinely grateful for the professional growth and relationships. Specifically, I want to acknowledge:

- The exceptional mentorship from you, Ms. Chen, which fundamentally shaped my leadership approach
- The opportunity to lead the digital transformation project, which increased our market reach by 40%
- The collaborative team environment and the talented professionals I've had the honor to work alongside
- The professional skills in project management, team leadership, and strategic planning

During my final month, I am committed to ensuring a smooth transition:

- I will document all marketing initiatives, timelines, and campaign status
- I am available to train my replacement on vendor relationships and platform management
- I will provide comprehensive documentation of my responsibilities and processes
- I am willing to assist in recruitment and onboarding if needed
- I am available for consultation on current projects after my departure

The relationships and experiences here have been invaluable to my professional journey. I have tremendous respect for InnovateTech's mission and wish the organization and team continued success.

Thank you for investing in my development and for the incredible opportunity to contribute to this organization's success.

Sincerely,
Michael Rodriguez
(555) 789-1234
michael.rodriguez@email.com
LinkedIn.com/in/michaelrodriguez
tips: Keep the tone professional and grateful throughout, even if you're leaving due to dissatisfaction.
Acknowledge specific people, projects, or achievements rather than using generic gratitude.
Be specific about your transition plan and offer concrete ways to help during the handoff period.
Provide sufficient notice (typically one month for professional/senior positions) when using this format.
Briefly explain your reason for departure but focus on your future rather than criticisms of the company.
Mention specific skills you've gained that you'll take forward in your career.
Offer post-departure availability for questions or consultation on critical matters.
Proofread carefully and have a trusted colleague review before submitting to leadership.
Deliver in person first, then follow up with formal written submission.
Keep a copy in your personal records for future reference.

faqs.question: Who should I send my long-form resignation letter to?
faqs.answer: Address it to your direct manager, but also include your HR department or other relevant leadership. For senior positions, you may address company leadership directly.

faqs.question: How much detail should I include about my reasons for leaving?
faqs.answer: Include enough to be respectful and transparent, but focus on your future rather than criticisms. For positive reasons (new opportunity, career growth), be specific. For negative reasons, keep it general.

faqs.question: Is a long-form resignation appropriate for all positions?
faqs.answer: Long-form resignations are most appropriate for senior positions, those with significant tenure, or when additional context benefits the organization. For junior roles, shorter letters are usually sufficient.

faqs.question: Should I include personal achievements in my resignation letter?
faqs.answer: Yes, mentioning specific projects or achievements you led helps the organization understand your contributions and can leave a positive lasting impression.

faqs.question: Can I mention specific people who mentored me?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Acknowledging mentors and leaders by name is appropriate and appreciated. It strengthens relationships and shows gratitude.

faqs.question: How long should a long-form resignation letter be?
faqs.answer: Typically 250-400 words, roughly 3/4 to 1 full page. It should be comprehensive but not excessive.

faqs.question: What if I'm leaving under negative circumstances?
faqs.answer: Even when leaving due to workplace issues, keep a long-form resignation professional. Focus on what you learned rather than complaints. Save detailed concerns for exit interviews if appropriate.

faqs.question: Should I discuss my new opportunity in detail?
faqs.answer: You can mention your new role and why it appeals to you, but avoid going into excessive detail. Keep the focus on your transition and gratitude rather than the new position.
